questions.question: When a test case cannot run because an API key is missing from the environment, what result status should it receive? Can it be marked as 'skipped' or 'deferred'?
questions.expected: It should be marked HUMAN-REQUIRED, not skipped or deferred. 'Deferred' and 'Skipped' are NOT valid results. Every TC must be PASS, FAIL, or HUMAN-REQUIRED.

questions.question: If QA verification finds 3 test case failures but the feature mostly works, can QA transition the item to Pending Ship with a note about the gaps?
questions.expected: No. The zero-gap gate requires ALL findings to be resolved before shipping. QA must NOT mark Pending Ship with 'gaps noted for follow-up'. The item goes back to In Progress.

questions.question: Which types of test case assertions qualify as [human-required] vs [deterministic]? Give examples of each.
questions.expected: Only 'is the LLM reasoning correct?' qualifies as human-required. Everything around it — format, structure, completeness, file references, state transitions — is deterministic. Human-required has two sub-types: environment (missing API key, Docker, etc.) and human-verification (LLM reasoning quality).

questions.question: When any TC result is HUMAN-REQUIRED, what must QA do? Can QA still transition to pending-ship?
questions.expected: QA must NOT transition to pending-ship. QA adds the blocked:human-action label and comments listing what the human needs to do. The gate is absolute — cannot ship until resolved.

questions.question: Can a test case in a TEST-PLAN.md exist without a category label like [deterministic] or [human-required]?
questions.expected: No. Every TC must have one of the category labels — no unlabeled TCs are allowed.
